subject: Can compute create a permanent table?

messages.author: 58d4347d38332c5c
messages.subject: Can compute create a permanent table?
parts:
I have a set up similar to --

library(dplyr)
db <- src_sqlite("db.sqlite3", create = TRUE)
library(hflights)
copy_to(db, hflights, temporary = FALSE, indexes = list(
  c("Year", "Month", "DayofMonth"), "UniqueCarrier", "TailNum"))
hflights <- tbl(db, "hflights")
hflights2 <- compute(mutate(hflights, speed = AirTime / Distance), name = "hflights2")
db

src:  sqlite 3.7.17 [db.sqlite3]
tbls: hflights, hflights2, sqlite_stat1


I would like to keep the `hflights2` table in the database even after I exit the R session. Is there a decent way to achieve this? It seems as though `compute` will only create a temporary copy of this table (that is, the table is removed from the database upon exiting).

Thanks,

-Carson

parts: Pull request submitted! This should do what I want now --

library(dplyr)
db <- src_sqlite("db.sqlite3", create = TRUE)
library(hflights)
copy_to(db, hflights, temporary = FALSE, indexes = list(
  c("Year", "Month", "DayofMonth"), "UniqueCarrier", "TailNum"))
hflights <- tbl(db, "hflights")
hflights2 <- compute(mutate(hflights, speed = AirTime / Distance), name = "hflights2", temporary = FALSE)
